note: The pool a title set is selected FROM, not the title set itself. Nothing here claims an availability tier: harness/census.py measures every entry against the configured indexers and harness/titles.py assigns the tier from what came back. proposed_tier records only why the entry was put in the pool, so a candidate that lands somewhere else is a finding rather than a mistake.
id_correctness_is_measured: A wrong IMDb id is the easiest way to poison a benchmark: it produces an honest zero from every target and reads as unavailability. The census keeps the top release names for every entry and titles.py flags any entry whose results do not contain a recognisable form of the expected title, so a bad id shows up as MISMATCH before a round rather than as five identical failures during one.

candidates.title: (unallocated id)
candidates.why: well-formed and almost certainly unallocated. Separates 'no release exists' from 'no title exists': an addon may legitimately behave differently on the two, and neither may be a 500.
